question.text: Karnataka Angel Collective invests INR 2 crore in NovaTech Seed-stage at a pre-money valuation of INR 18 crore (8 lakh shares issued to existing holders; Karnataka buys new shares at face value after pre-money 18 cr = INR 225/share × 8 lakh). One year later NovaTech does a down-round Series A at INR 150/share. Karnataka has a Broad-Based Weighted Average anti-dilution clause with 10 lakh fully-diluted shares and a new-round issue of 4 lakh shares at INR 150. What is Karnataka's adjusted conversion price (approx.)?

answer.text: INR 225.00 — no adjustment since clause never triggers.

explanation.text: The Logic: Broad-based weighted-average formula: NCP = OCP × (A + B) / (A + C), where OCP = INR 225, A = 10 lakh (fully diluted pre-round shares), B = consideration received / OCP = (4 lakh × 150) / 225 = 6 lakh × 100/225 ≈ 2.667 lakh, C = 4 lakh shares actually issued. NCP = 225 × (10 + 2.667) / (10 + 4) = 225 × 12.667 / 14 = 225 × 0.9048 ≈ INR 203.57. The Trap: Option A is the full-ratchet answer (resets to new round price — founder-hostile). Option B assumes the clause never triggers — wrong, it triggers on any down-round. Option D swaps broad-based with narrow-based (narrow uses a smaller A, so gives a lower NCP). Cross-Exam Context: XV (Research Analyst) tests anti-dilution math in cap-table modelling. XIX-A distributor level tests only the concept, not the math. XXI-B (PM) is listed-only and doesn't test this.
